analysis:
This PR is documentation-only: docs/developer/test.md (date stamp at line 3 and new test descriptions at lines 173-180) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (date stamp and the reasoning control row near lines 1147-1153). I examined all supplied units against the threat model (TB-002, TB-007, T-041 and the TB-011 App Attest assets) and found no code, key-handling, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage change.

The test.md additions only name existing GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests cases that replay OpenRouter-captured requests. They introduce no new runtime surface, and the surrounding text keeps the fixed-vector and synthetic-evidence limits.

The protocol-messages.md change documents reasoning-control parsing in GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift. Null `reasoning` and null members are treated as unset. `reasoning.summary` and `reasoning.generate_summary` accept auto, concise or detailed as no-ops, and other `reasoning` members are refused. Only the first row's patch excerpt was visible, and it was truncated. The document claims strict refusal, but the implementation was not supplied, so it cannot be verified here. The no-op summary values should not enable reasoning-summary output or leak withheld reasoning. This is a documentation claim about input validation, not an observed regression, and it does not change any T-041 cache or at-rest posture.

The remaining open question is whether the provider source actually matches the documented refusal behavior. That belongs to a code-bearing review, not this docs-only change.
